text: Checking whether splitters are unlocked; that decides how coal gets back off the iron belt at base.

I'd put coal on the empty lane of the existing iron-plate belt, which already runs from the furnaces to base, and pull it back off at base with a filter splitter. It needs about **107 belts** (74 at the coal field + 29 at base + 4 inside the splitter), so your 128 leaves about 20 spare for going around trees. A dedicated belt all the way to the boilers would be about 220 belts, more than your 128 plus the ~62 you could craft from 94 iron.

**What the existing belts are:** the y=-26 belt is the iron-plate line. It starts at (71.5,45.5) next to the furnace column, runs north up x=71.5, then west along y=-25.5 to (-21.5,-25.5). Furnace output inserters drop plates only on its west lane, so the east lane is empty. Coal that enters on that lane stays on it through both turns and reaches base on the north lane. The coal belt at y=101-103 carries coal west to the copper area, away from base, so it's no use here.

**Two things to check before you start:**
- Whether the crew can set a filter on a splitter. If not, stop and ask me; an unfiltered splitter would push iron plates onto the boiler belt and choke it.
- The corner belt at (71.5,-25.5). The map draws it pointing north (^) while the next tile (70.5,-25.5) points west. Look at it: if it really points north, the line dead-ends there, which would explain why the furnace output inserters say "waiting for space". Rotate it to point west.

**Materials:** 2 electric mining drills, 1 splitter, 1 inserter, 2 small electric poles, ~110 belts. Crafting those takes about 60 iron (you have 94) and about 20 copper. Bring the copper.

**A. Coal pickup (at the coal patch)**
1. Electric drill at (49.5,96.5), facing east.
2. Electric drill at (49.5,99.5), facing east.
   - Both drop onto the belt at x=51.5, on its east lane.
   - Together they give 1.0 coal/s. Two boilers at full load burn 0.9/s.
3. Small poles:
   - (44.5,101.5): connects to the existing pole at (42.5,105.5).
   - (47.5,97.5): powers both drills.
4. Belt north along x=51.5 from y=99.5 to y=47.5: 53 belts.
   - Trees to mine on that column: (51.5,96.5), (51.5,94.5), (51.5,92.5), (51.5,88.5), (51.5,83.5), (51.5,81.5). Or use `connect` to go around them.
5. Corner at (51.5,46.5) facing east, then east along y=46.5 to x=70.5, then (71.5,46.5) facing north: 21 belts.
   - The last belt joins the back of the plate belt (71.5,45.5) head-on, not from the side, so the lanes don't mix.

**B. Pulling the coal off at base**
6. Mine the belt at (-17.5,-25.5). Place the splitter at (-17.5,-25) facing west.
   - Filter: coal, output priority left (south).
   - Coal comes out at (-18.5,-24.5). Iron carries on west at (-18.5,-25.5) as before.
   - Both iron-chest inserters, at (-19.5,-26.5) and (-22.5,-25.5), are past the splitter, so they only ever see iron.
7. Belt west along y=-24.5 from x=-18.5 to x=-26.5: 9 belts.
8. (-27.5,-24.5) facing north, then north along x=-27.5 from y=-25.5 to y=-38.5: 15 belts.
9. Mine the wooden chest at (-27.5,-39.5) and put a belt there facing west. The existing inserter at (-27.5,-40.5) now takes coal from it into the boiler at (-27,-42.5).
10. North along x=-28.5 from y=-39.5 to y=-42.5: 4 belts. The belt just ends at (-28.5,-42.5).
11. New inserter at (-29.5,-42.5) facing east. It takes from the belt at (-28.5,-42.5) and drops into the boiler at (-31.5,-43).

**Build order:** B first (6–11), because it's next to you and the boilers can still be hand-fed meanwhile. Then walk south and build A (1–5).

When coal backs up on the boiler belt, the splitter holds it back on the coal lane and the plates keep moving. Once the coal lane is full all the way back, the drills stop until the boilers need more.

text:
I laid the copper smelter and the coal hookup as ghosts: 60 in total, 55 at base and 5 at the coal end. Fuel comes from the dead-end coal belt, which I sideload onto the empty north lane of the ore belt. Six stone furnaces give 1.875 copper/s, above the 1.5/s roadmap target.

**To bring:** 36 belts, 6 stone furnaces, 12 inserters, 6 small poles. That covers the 60 ghosts plus your existing belt at (23.5,103.5), which gets turned north. Each furnace uses about 0.02 coal/s.

**A. Smelter at the ore belt end (ghosts placed)**
1. **Ore belt:** extend it north from (3.5,-13.5) to (3.5,-23.5), all facing north (11 belts). It ends there, two tiles short of the iron belt.
   - You're standing at (3.5,-13.5); step off it.
   - Ore stays on the west lane and coal arrives on the east lane. Both lanes back up, which is what you want.
2. **Furnaces:** 2x2 stone furnaces at (1,-14), (1,-16), (1,-18), (1,-20), (1,-22), (1,-24).
3. **Input inserters:** at x=2.5, y = -13.5, -15.5, -17.5, -19.5, -21.5, -23.5, all facing east. They take ore and coal from the belt and drop into the furnaces. Furnace inserters load coal as fuel by themselves, so no separate fuel line is needed.
4. **Output inserters:** at x=-0.5, same y values, also facing east. They take plates from the furnaces and drop them onto x=-1.5.
5. **Poles:** small poles at (2.5,-14.5), (2.5,-18.5), (2.5,-22.5), (-0.5,-14.5), (-0.5,-18.5), (-0.5,-22.5). You need both columns because one pole can't reach across a furnace. (2.5,-22.5) connects to the existing pole at (0.5,-26.5).
6. **Plate belt:**
   - North along x=-1.5 from y=-13.5 to y=-23.5 (11 belts).
   - Corner at (-1.5,-24.5) facing west.
   - West along y=-24.5 to (-9.5,-24.5) (8 more belts).
   - Extend it west once the lead confirms the delivery point.
   - All of x=-2..3, y=-25..-13 was clear on the map.

**B. Coal onto the ore belt's north lane (at the copper patch)**
7. Rotate your existing belt at (23.5,103.5) to face north. Mine the dead-end belt at (22.5,103.5).
8. Mine the tree at (23.5,102.5), then build the ghost belts:
   - (23.5,102.5) north
   - (23.5,101.5) north
   - (23.5,100.5) west
   - (22.5,100.5) west
   - (21.5,100.5) south
   
   The last one feeds into the side of the ore belt at (21.5,101.5). Since there is belt upstream of that tile, it's a true sideload and all the coal lands on the north lane. The ore stays on its south lane.
   - Don't join at (22.5,101.5). That's the first tile of the ore belt, so joining there just bends the belt and both lanes of the coal belt carry straight on, putting coal on the ore lane too.
9. Coal takes about 75 seconds to travel up the belt. Hand-insert about 5 coal into each furnace to get them running now.

**C. Clash with my boiler-coal plan on y=-24.5**
- The boiler-coal splitter sits at (-17.5,-25). Its south input tile (-16.5,-24.5) must stay empty, or copper gets into the iron line.
- So the copper belt can run west along y=-24.5 as far as (-15.5,-24.5) and no further.
- The coal belt keeps y=-24.5 from x=-18.5 westward. Nothing overlaps.

**D. Correction to my boiler-coal plan**
Your ore belt shows that drills drop onto the near lane, not the far lane as I'd assumed. So drills at (49.5,96.5) and (49.5,99.5) facing east would put coal on the west lane of x=51.5, the same lane as the iron plates. That still works, because the splitter filters by item, but coal would be squeezed onto the plate lane. To keep coal on its own lane, join the plate belt from the side instead of head-on:
- Bring the coal belt east along y=48.5 to (72.5,48.5).
- Then (72.5,48.5) north, (72.5,47.5) north, (72.5,46.5) west.
- Add a one-belt stub at (71.5,47.5) facing north, plus (71.5,46.5) facing north.

The coal then goes onto the east lane of the plate belt. That's about 3 more belts. Claude-2's own note mentions a coal drill at (51,101) feeding coal into the ore belt at x=76; check that the two of you aren't building the same thing.

I haven't posted anything to the board. Build with `build_ghosts`.

I also found why the iron belt is empty: the corner belt at (71.5,-25.5) faces north into a dead end. All 11 iron furnaces are full with 100 plates each, and rotating that one belt to face west should send about 2.7 iron/s to the base. That fix is task #3.

**Ratios** (assembler-1 at speed 0.5):
- **Green:** 15/min needs 3 assemblers (5/min each).
- **Red:** 3 assemblers (6/min each, so 18/min).
- **Intermediates:** 1 inserter assembler, 2 belt assemblers (they hand belts straight to the greens), 1 gear (needs 0.625/s), 1 circuit, 1 cable.

- **Plates:** 1.875 iron/s and 0.625 copper/s (38/min). That's about 6 iron furnaces' worth (the x=74 column has 11) and 2 copper furnaces at minimum; plan on 4.

**(1) Where plates come from**
- **Iron:** furnaces at x=74 → belt north up x=71.5 → west along y=-25.5. I'm calling this belt M; it's the block's iron input and needs no changes.
- **Copper:** the copper field at (5,88) puts plates on the existing belt at x=0.5. Extend it north to (0.5,-22.5), east along y=-22.5 to x=48.5, then north under belt M with an underground pair: entrance at (48.5,-24.5), exit at (48.5,-26.5). From there a short feeder belt joins belt B1 from the side, which keeps copper on one lane. That's about 151 belts plus 1 underground pair (task #6).
- **Iron for the belt assemblers:** an inserter at (50.5,-26.5) lifts iron off belt M onto a feeder up to belt B2 (also from the side, one lane).

**(2) Block layout**, x=9..56, y=-40..-26. Belts B1/B2 run west; S1/S2 run east.

| Row | y | What's there |
|---|---|---|
| M | -25.5 | iron belt (existing) |
| inserters | -26.5 | take iron off M, facing south |
| Row A assemblers | -28.5 | gear 46.5, inserter 42.5, circuit 38.5, cable 34.5; cable→circuit→inserter hand off directly through inserters at 36.5 and 40.5 |
| inserters | -30.5 | gears onto B1, copper and gears off B1; a long inserter puts inserters onto B2 |
| B1 | -31.5 | gears (north lane) + copper (south lane) |
| B2 | -32.5 | inserters (north lane) + iron (south lane) |
| inserters | -33.5 | normal ones pick from B2, long ones from B1 |
| Row B assemblers | -35.5 | green 38.5, belt 34.5, green 30.5, belt 26.5, green 22.5, red 18.5 / 14.5 / 10.5; belt assemblers feed greens via inserters at 36.5, 32.5 and 24.5 |
| inserters | -37.5 | reds out with normal inserters, greens out with long ones |
| S1 | -38.5 | red packs |
| S2 | -39.5 | green packs |

Each belt carries only one item type per lane, so it can't jam with mixed items. First mine the rocks at about (18.5,-38.5) and (19.5,-35.5); they sit on the layout.

**(3) Labs:** 4 labs at y=-35.5, x=42.5 / 46.5 / 50.5 / 54.5, on the S1/S2 run east of the last green. Each has a normal inserter for red and a long inserter for green at y=-37.5, both facing north. Move the 2 existing labs there and craft 2 new ones.
- 4 labs use 15/min at techs of about 16s per unit; 30s techs need 8 labs.
- To get to 8, put 4 more above the belts: centers at y=-42.5, inserters at y=-40.5 facing south.

**Bill of materials**
- **Block:** 12 assembler-1, 4 lab, 24 inserter, 13 long-handed inserter, 15 small poles, 163 belts.
- **Copper line:** about 151 belts + 1 underground pair.
- **Belt supply:** there are 237 belts in the chest at (-12.5,-30.5), so craft about 80 more.
- **Circuits:** about 65, which takes about 100 copper. Have claude-4/5 hand-carry around 150 copper plates as soon as possible.

**Board tasks**
- **#3, claude-3:** rotate the corner belt at (71.5,-25.5) to face west. Do this first.
- **#4, claude-1:** build the block ghosts (assemblers, inserters, poles, labs), reusing the old chest-fed assemblers and labs.
- **#5, claude-2:** belts B1/B2/S1/S2 and the two feeders, then craft long inserters, assemblers and labs.
- **#6, claude-3:** the copper belt from (0.5,78.5) to the underground at x=48.5.

M dead-ends at the boilers and nothing there uses iron, so that lane fills up with iron and the coal behind it can't move.

**Fix A: move coal to M's north lane (do now, 5 changes).**
1. Mine the underground-belt pair at (72.5,23.5) and (70.5,23.5).
2. Mine the transport-belts at (69.5,23.5), (69.5,22.5) and (70.5,22.5).
